info.title: Job Hunt OS
info.description: Evidence-grounded career decision-and-execution system. The Career Evidence Bank in data/*.yaml is the authoritative source of truth.

get.description:
Ranked, filtered, sorted jobs, paginated.

``relevant_only`` defaults True: a real board is mostly roles that failed
deterministic screening (sales, support, non-US, too senior). Showing them
by default buries the handful that matter. Set it False, or pass
``crm_state=REJECTED``, to see them — "Show rejected" in the UI is this
flag, not a separate code path.

post.description: Store an outreach draft. This never sends anything.
Record that *the user* sent a draft. The system cannot set this itself.
Record a referral state. Duplicate asks warn; they are never blocked.

get.description: Vocabulary for the frontend, so no list is hand-copied into React.
The configured watchlist. Reads the config file; touches no network.

One cheap read per configured source. Ingests nothing.

This *does* reach the network, which is why it is opt-in per request rather
than part of the watchlist view.

Recently discovered jobs from automated collection.

Manual imports are excluded: this answers "what did automation find",
which is the question the dashboard section asks.

post.description:
Steps A-F of Slice 5 §6: guard, choose base, parse, map evidence,
propose defensible tailoring, run SafeClaimValidator.

Does not alter a source resume — it produces (or refreshes) a review
screen's worth of ``ResumeRecommendation`` rows and returns the guard
result alongside them. A blocked job raises 422 with the reason rather
than silently returning nothing, so the UI can show *why*.

Renders only rows the user explicitly accepted. Rejects and pending
rows are excluded — nothing defaults onto the document.

Requires an application date and a resume version — the UI collects
both before this fires. Sending is always external; this only records
that the user did it themselves.

get.description:
The complete base resume for a role family, before tailoring.

Lets the review screen distinguish BASE RESUME from TAILORING CHANGES, so
a list of seven proposed edits does not read as the whole document.

It is the Resume Library document: built with no job, through the same
builder and claim gate as a job resume, and fitted to one page - so the
preview, the download and the base a job tailors all agree.

How this posting is being positioned, and what that did to the resume.

A GET so the Resume tab can render the explanation on first load without
POSTing anything. Building a profile and a base resume is pure computation
over the Evidence Bank — no writes, no LLM, no network.

post.description:
Import a listing the user found themselves.

Three shapes, chosen by what the payload carries:

* ``save_url_only`` — record the link and the user's own words for company
  and title. Nothing is inferred about the role.
* a ``description`` — the paste fallback, for pages that cannot be read.
* neither — fetch and extract the URL under the SSRF guards.

``intent`` decides the post-import state and is applied through the normal
append-only transition system. Nothing here marks a job applied.

Record an application the user submitted outside Job Hunt OS.

This is the point of manual import for a job already in flight: the Job Hunt
OS should be the source of truth for the search even when it neither
discovered the job nor produced the resume. It uses the same append-only
transition system as everything else — no raw status update.

get.description:
The most urgent next step across the pipeline.

``source=USER_ADDED`` filters to jobs the user imported. That is a filter,
not a separate feature: imported jobs appear in every other list too, which
is the whole point of routing them through the same pipeline.
How fresh the corpus is, what is monitored, and what ran last.

post.description: Start a structured collection now. Refuses if one is already running.

get.description:
What a local schedule would look like. This endpoint registers nothing.

Registration touches the operating system's scheduler, which is a change to
the machine rather than to this application's data. It happens from the CLI,
after the user reads the command.

post.description: Start polling one employer's board, because the user asked.

get.description:
Every registry company with its derived health, plus coverage totals.

Read-only. Health comes from recorded polls; nothing here touches a board.

post.description:
Add an employer from its careers URL, because the user asked.

Detection runs again here rather than trusting a provider or board sent by
the page: the browser never decides what a board is. Only a CONFIRMED board
is monitored. Anything else is stored only when the user asked to keep it
as manual-only, so the gap stays visible.

What a careers URL is, and whether it can be monitored. Writes nothing.

At most one request to the board the URL names, and one fetch of the page
itself (through the same guarded fetcher URL import uses).

Pause or resume one registry company. Seed companies included; the
curated file is never edited.
One cheap read of a registry company's board. Ingests nothing.

get.description: Everything the People page shows, counted from records.

post.description: A human heard back. Never inferred — silence is not a reply.

get.description:
Who to contact about this job: people already known, plus searches to run.

Returns strings. Nothing is fetched, no account is used, and the user picks
the actual person.

post.description: Link an existing contact to this job. One person, many roles.

Compose a draft from recorded facts and store it.

Storing it is not sending it: `sent_by_user` stays False until a human says
otherwise, and there is no transport in this process.
Record that *the user* sent this, and set the follow-up reminder.
Push a reminder out. It stays open — snoozing is not completing.

get.description: Overdue / today / next 7 days, split so the page does not re-derive it.

schema.title: Response Networking Follow Ups Api Follow Ups Networking Get

get.description: Everything the Application tab needs to show the cover-letter row.

post.description: Compose a letter from the Evidence Bank and render both formats.

Persist the user's own wording, and re-render from it.

The saved text is what gets rendered — the user's edit is the document from
here on, not a note attached to the generated one.

Record that a letter written elsewhere was used.

The same path an external resume takes: the system tracks that the document
exists so readiness is honest, without pretending to hold a copy of it.

The complete base resume, before any job tailoring.

Exposed so the UI can show what the proposed changes actually modify —
seven changes are edits to this document, not the document itself.

ExternalCoverLetterPayload.title: ExternalCoverLetterPayload

GenerateBaseResumeResponse.description: A base rendered on its own - no Job, Application or ResumeVersion.

GenerateCoverLetterPayload.title: GenerateCoverLetterPayload
GenerateCoverLetterPayload.description: Everything optional here is opt-IN, and each choice is recorded.

JobRow.title: JobRow

PeopleSummaryResponse.title: PeopleSummaryResponse
PeopleSummaryResponse.description: The People page: KPIs counted from records, plus its four sections.

RegistryCompanyView.title: RegistryCompanyView

ScheduleSetupResponse.title: ScheduleSetupResponse
ScheduleSetupResponse.description: What a local schedule would look like. Registers nothing.

SearchStrategyView.title: SearchStrategyView
SearchStrategyView.description: A search a human runs. Nothing here fetches anything.

SourceDetectionResponse.title: SourceDetectionResponse
SourceDetectionResponse.description: What a careers URL resolves to. Detecting writes nothing.

SweepView.title: SweepView
SweepView.description: The last GROUP of runs. One `collection_run` row is one company.

TargetingAuditView.title: TargetingAuditView
TargetingAuditView.description: Internal QA. NOT an ATS score and never presented as one.

TargetingExplanationView.title: TargetingExplanationView
TargetingExplanationView.description:
The "why this resume looks different" panel.

Deliberately excludes the scoring weights and per-bullet dimensions. Those
exist (see ``resume_targeting.BulletScore``) and are useful in tests and the
audit, but a review screen that leads with a formula invites the user to
tune the formula instead of reading the resume.

TestSourceResponse.title: TestSourceResponse
TestSourceResponse.description: One cheap read of a registry company's board. Ingests nothing.

TimelineEntryView.title: TimelineEntryView
TimelineEntryView.description:
One status change.

``from`` is a Python keyword, so the field is declared as ``from_`` and
aliased. ``serialization_alias`` keeps the JSON key as ``from`` — the
frontend and the OpenAPI document both see the natural name.

WhyMissedResponse.title: WhyMissedResponse
WhyMissedResponse.description:
Why automated discovery did not find a manually added job.

Every field is derived from stored provenance and collection history. When
the recorded facts support no reason, `reason` is UNKNOWN and says so.

WhyThisMatchesView.title: WhyThisMatchesView
WhyThisMatchesView.description:
The user-facing explanation of a functional match.

Evidence of the classifier's reasoning, not of the candidate's fitness.
Internal scoring never appears here.
